newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-ANGRY ROTOR SAY DRUNK LINESMAN COST THEM VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANGRY ROTOR SAY DRUNK LINESMAN COST THEM VICTORY.

text.p: Russian title contenders Rotor Volgograd say they were robbed of a crucial victory by a drunk linesman who ruled out a perfectly good goal, Itar-Tass news agency reported on Monday.

Rotor were top of the table when they went into Saturday's game at strugglers Chernomorets Novorossiisk but managed only a goalless draw, allowing Spartak Moscow to go one point ahead with just two games left.
Rotor thought they had scored when Gennady Yesipov headed home from close range in the 19th minute but the goal was ruled out.
"The team thinks the linesman was not in a sober state during the match. The goal was disallowed after his flag went up," Tass reported from Volgograd.
Rotor president Vladimir Goryunov tried to investigate his players' allegations at the end of the game but was told by the match inspector nothing was amiss, the agency said.
Goryunov tried to take the matter further, at which point Chernomorets said he was the one who was drunk. Goryunov denied the charges and has threatened to sue his accusers.

An official at the Russian referees' organisation said the matter would be raised at the soccer league's disciplinary committee on Tuesday but strongly denied Rotor's accusations, saying the team were trying to obscure their own failings.
"This whole row has blown up because Rotor have been playing badly away from home recently and have not scored enough goals," Nikolai Zhikharev said.
Russian teams regularly complain about refereeing decisions which go against them and usually accuse the officials of being incompetent or corrupt.
